utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everyone in and around this courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Thank you, Your Honour. This is case number IT-03-69-T, the Prosecutor versus Jovica Stanisic and Franko Simatovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Mr. Jordash, first of all, I establish that Mr. Stanisic is not present in court. I -- the Chamber was informed that Mr. Stanisic was sent to hospital urgently because he had kidney stones again and that he needed treatment urgently and that the expectation is that he will return to the UNDU today, this afternoon. I don't know whether he has returned already. Which then, of course, raises the question of whether we can proceed in his absence or not. We have not received a waiver form. We were informed that Mr. Stanisic -- that it would be difficult anyhow to fill in a waiver form at this moment. And, therefore, the Chamber is unaware of the position Mr. Stanisic would like to take, if he had a waiver form, whether he would fill it in and sign it or whether he would prefer that we suspend the proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Mr. Knoops spoke to him this morning, late morning, and he confirmed that he wished to be present and wasn't wanting to wave his right to be present.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. That's -- that's -- we were hearing the evidence. Now, apart from hearing evidence, we also had a few procedural issues. I do not know whether we could deal with those. They are relatively simple, I would say. Perhaps I just list them so that you can consider whether or not it would be in accordance with the instructions you received that we could deal with those procedural issues, yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I had -- the first one is to hear a response by the Prosecution in relation to the request to put certain questions to Dr. Eekhof. That would be one of the procedural matters. The second one would be to verify whether the other parties in this proceedings would agree with you, Mr. Jordash, that the meeting on medical records which is scheduled for tomorrow should be held in the absence of any other party, that is, Chamber being represented, Registrar, and Stanisic Defence. This may sound a bit mysterious for those who have not followed the brief e-mail exchange between the Chamber and Mr. Jordash. As you may remember, Mr. Jordash has raised an issue of access to medical records. The Chamber then suggested to discuss this with the Registry. A meeting for that purpose has been scheduled for tomorrow, and Mr. Jordash took the position that this was a matter between Registry and Stanisic Defence and although the Chamber being present, that it was not a matter which -- in which the other parties would have any right of presence. We are talking about how to get access to the medical records. That's basic. Mr. Groome, would you agree -- would you insist on being present, or would you share with Mr. Jordash that -- the view of Mr. Jordash that the other parties would have no role to play in such a conversation?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I believe I sent an e-mail stating the Prosecution's position on this. We accept that we do not have a role, except for the situation where Mr. Jordash would then want to take some of those medical records and make them the basis of some other application; in that case, then we would suggest that we do have a right to see whatever portion of medical records are advanced on a relevant issue in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think the issue to be discussed is how do we get the records from the doctors. And, of course, if Mr. Jordash wants to rely on them at any stage, then, of course, he would have to submit them, if you want to rely upon them. And then, of course, questions as whether these are all the records, or part of it, or what the selection is based, of course, may then become a relevant issue. But I'm not yet that far. The meeting is, at this moment, exclusively about how to do we get them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And the Prosecution makes no request to be at that initial meeting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, as far as the Simatovic Defence is concerned, we accept what you said. We don't insist on the presence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Jordash, I introduced the matter in order for you to express your view on whether we could deal with that matter in the absence of Mr. Stanisic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I'm confident we can, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have, as a matter of fact, more or less, done it already. So that's, then, at least, not an item that we have to further discuss. Finally, we -- there is -- the Chamber would like to give some guidance in relation to bar table submissions. Is that guidance that you think you could receive in the absence of Mr. Stanisic, or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we have identified the procedural items. Let's go back, then, to them. The first one was -- and there I haven't heard your views, I think, Mr. Jordash, whether we could receive the response of the Prosecution on your request to put certain questions to Dr. Eekhof. Should the Chamber hear that in the absence of Mr. Stanisic or should we not?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Given the position that Mr. Stanisic has taken in the past, I think I can generally say that we can proceed with all procedural matters. I will leap to my feet if I consider the opposite is the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good. I have identified, now, all that are on my list. Mr. Groome, are you already in a position to tell us whether you want to respond to the request to ask questions to Dr. Eekhof in relation to the possibly increasing sitting days, and if so, whether you are able to give it now orally or whether would you do it in any other way?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, could I ask that we be allowed to make a written submission on that, and I could have that to the Chamber by tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: By tomorrow morning. That seems ... Does the Simatovic Defence take any position in relation to the questions and the request to put them to Dr. Eekhof, or do you stay out of the matter?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I put a rather ambiguous question. First, whether you take any position. I took the answer "no" to that first question and not to the second question, which was whether you stayed out of that. And I do understand that you want to stay out of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right, Your Honour, you have understood correctly, and I apologise for being unclear myself. So we don't have a position, and we do not wish to attend -- to take part. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I usually blame the one who puts the ambiguous questions for any confusion, so I'm blaming myself. Then we have dealt with the -- who will be present at the meeting tomorrow. We've dealt with that. Then, finally, I'd like to deliver a further guidance in relation to bar table submissions. There has been an out-of-court meeting last week between the parties and Chamber's staff discussing in which form the per diem documents should be submitted. Also last week, the Chamber informally received a memo from the Prosecution on its understanding of how bar table documents should be submitted to the Chamber. And in response to that, I would like to give the following guidance on behalf of the Chamber: First, if the parties want to tender documents, they should preferably do so during examinations of witnesses who may give meaningful context to the documents. Second, if there is no witness who could contextualise the document, the parties can bar table that document by creating a spreadsheet. That could be one document or more related documents. That spreadsheet should, first of all, describe the document. It should indicate relevance and should point to specific portions if the documents are lengthy documents. And they should leave one free column for the other party for objections or comments. If it would, therefore, be a Prosecution motion -- or a Prosecution spreadsheet, then they should leave one column open for the Defence. Or for the two Defence teams, I would say two columns. Now, after that chart is completed, which means that it includes any comments or any objections by the Defence if they wish to do so, then that chart should be filed. And the Chamber will then subsequently decide on admission of those bar table documents. Third, if the parties have a number of similar documents, they are not required to ask a witness the same questions for each document but could do so for two or three documents as examples and then bar table the rest. In such a scenario, the relevance and the contextualisation is sufficiently clear and no spreadsheet would need to be filed. Having given this guidance, I do understand that the parties have agreed to file a spreadsheet for the per diem lists. So in this instance, we will await the filing of the spreadsheet. And this concludes the Chamber's guidance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I may have created some confusion in respect of the following: There were two issues where I invited the Simatovic Defence to give their position. The first one was about the presence tomorrow during that meeting. I think that answer is clear that you do not seek to be present. Now, the questions to be put to Dr. Eekhof was a different matter. I understood - but perhaps I've not been clear there - that you also did not wish to be a party in that discussion. The matter on which the Prosecution said that it would respond in writing by tomorrow, do you want to respond as well, or do you also stay out of that matter? You may have seen that the request --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. We'll reserve the right to state our position in due course. I apologise for interrupting you if you haven't finished what you were saying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you say we still may want to express our views, your views then, on what questions to be put to Dr. Eekhof? Because there were two issues. The first is: How do we get access to medical records. That will be discussed during a meeting tomorrow. You do not wish to be present there. The second issue was in relation to possibly sitting more days a week that Mr. Jordash filed a request that certain questions would be put to Dr. Eekhof. Mr. Jordash, correct me when I'm wrong, but I think there were three specific questions, and then you wanted us to remind Dr. Eekhof of certain consequences of sitting more. There the Prosecution said that it would respond in writing to be submitted tomorrow. And it's not entirely clear whether the Simatovic Defence wants to play a role in that discussion as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Simatovic Defence does not wish to participate in the discussion with respect to the health of Mr. Stanisic and how his health will affect the further course of this trial. When I said that we reserve the right to make a response, I meant with respect to the 9th of July and the dead-line when we are to state our position with respect to the change in the modalities of the trial proceedings from September onwards. And so the Simatovic Defence will do this by the 9th of July, presenting its arguments without entering into discussions of Mr. Stanisic's health, which is up to the Stanisic Defence team and not the Simatovic Defence team. And I hope that makes our position clearer now, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that makes your position clear that you would like to express your views on the question how to proceed without specifically discussing what questions should be put to what doctors at what time in relation to Mr. Stanisic's health; is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, precisely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bakrac for this clarification. Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, could I return to the issue of bar tables and -- just to seek some clarification on the guidance the Chamber's just provided?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What problem, Your Honour, that I see - and I'd ask the Chamber to clarify - is in the procedure for a written bar table submission. It seems that the Chamber has envisaged that the Prosecution would provide a chart to the Defence on which they could note their position and then we would file it jointly. One issue that I see with that is that in that informal pre-filing of any motion process, there's no time-limit on that. And we are advancing in the Prosecution case, and the Prosecution would appreciate that either the Chamber put some definite time-limit on it - and I would suggest the two weeks ordinarily given to respond would be a reasonable one or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you would say once the Prosecution has disclosed to the Defence the chart with the one or the two columns not yet being filled, that two weeks would be sufficient for -- you would consider two weeks a reasonable time for them to either object or to point at other relevant pages or give comments on whatever the Prosecution has introduced?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, it does depend on the size of the proposal. I mean, what I would propose instead is that we, the parties who have co-operated relatively well, I think, up to now, look at the size of the proposal by the opposing party and come to an informal agreement with the enforcement being that the party can say, Well, we are going to file it because you haven't responded to us in the agreed time. Or if an agreement cannot be reached between the parties, we then revert to the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I completely agree with Mr. Jordash. And I don't need to repeat our problems. You know that there are certain issues that we can respond to quickly and easily, but then again there are others which require more time and thought in view of our situation. So that from our position my learned friend Mr. Jordash's proposal is all the more pertinent so that we can see whether we can respond to certain questions in a short space of time or whether we are going to need more time. And we'll let you know in due course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, high expectations of your good co-operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... and I accept the representations of the Defence. And if there are any problems, I will return to the Chamber and ask for additional relief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And one other matter with respect to this, Your Honour. It seems that when the Chamber has talked about working with bar table submissions with witnesses it has not talked about a chart but it has mentioned that in cases of a large number of similar documents it may be that just a couple are actually led with the witness. It seems that in that situation a chart would also be helpful to the Chamber --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, what we have seen, and that's, of course, slightly different -- is a slightly different situation is that a witness who was able to say something about authenticity or recognition of handwriting, et cetera, that he would fill in a chart but then give evidence that the chart he filled in, that he looked at all of those documents which are in that chart and that he put his comments on there. Which is, of course, slightly different because a bar table document is mainly where we do not receive any additional evidence from that witness on that document, whereas here it's more or less a stream-lined presentation of the evidence of that witness in relation to certain documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So is it my understanding that the Chamber appreciates that type of document or would prefer not to have a document where the witness has included some comments about their observations of documents?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber appreciates how it was done in the past, but, of course, it was slightly different from just bar tabling documents. Bar tabling documents meaning, Here are the documents, look at that and that and that, and that's the parties' submissions, what is relevant, why it is relevant, what pages there are. And then that's slightly different from the kind of charts we have received where witnesses say, I've looked at 20 documents, I recognised on 18 out of 20 the handwriting, I indicated that. That was appreciated was a very efficient way of presenting that evidence. And, of course, the witness can be cross-examined on it, which is usually not the case with a pure bar table document.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I understand now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any other questions?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber has decided that we'll not further proceed today. However, the Chamber would like to inform the witness who has been waiting of the present situation and also explain that it may be uncertain as whether we can proceed tomorrow. It will depend on the condition of your client, Mr. Jordash. And either he comes to court or whether he wishes to attend the hearing through videolink or whether he wants to waive his right; all the options are open for tomorrow. But the Chamber would like to explain that to the witness at this moment. Protective measures are effective, which is pseudonym, face distortion. Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, while we are waiting for the witness to be brought in, the second witness for the week has arrived in The Hague, so I would ask to the Chamber to consider whether there's a possibility of sitting other days this week should Mr. Stanisic's health improve. And if we're not, I appreciate if the Prosecution could be informed so we could send him back to his --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll explore those possibilities. And, of course, much depends also on what the condition of Mr. Stanisic will be tomorrow. Would it be one day, are there any other courtrooms available, are there any other reasons that would oppose.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness JF-050. Please be seated. Witness JF-050, unfortunately, due to the medical condition of one of the accused, we cannot proceed -- is there any -- can you hear me? Apparently not. Could we --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. I can hear you, I can hear you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. So due to the medical condition of one of the accused, we cannot proceed today. I don't know whether you are aware of a -- kind of a basic rule in criminal procedure that an accused has the right to be present when he is tried. So if he is, for medical reasons, unavailable, the Chamber has to decide whether or not to proceed in his absence. And the Chamber has decided that we'll not proceed at this moment in his absence, which also means that we cannot hear your evidence today. It is still uncertain what the situation will be tomorrow. Perhaps we can proceed tomorrow, but that's not for certain yet. I'd like to instruct you that you still should not speak with anyone about your testimony, whether to be given or whether already given. And we'll keep you informed through the Victims and Witness Section on the developments. So whether we'll see you back tomorrow or not is still uncertain, but the Chamber preferred to explain it to you in person what the reason is that we cannot hear your evidence this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I don't see a problem there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, then, very much. The witness can be escorted out of the courtroom again. Thank you. We might see you back tomorrow or at any later stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there any other matter any party would like to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Not from the Prosecution, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and I see two times nodding no from the Defence teams. We then adjourn for the day. And we will resume tomorrow, the 6th of July, quarter past 2 in the afternoon in this same courtroom, unless the parties receive information that we still cannot proceed, in which case, we'll further inform the parties and the public when we will resume. We stand adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 6th day of July, 2010, at 2.15 p.m. 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 3.01 p.m.,
